title: Kabi Kabi language and place names

points: Wunya ngulum (say one-ya nulem): welcome everyone.
Weyba: understood to mean place of stingrays. Lots of local names end in -ba, which means place.
Noosa: from Noothera or Gnuthuru, understood to mean shadow or shady place. Noosa Head was Wantima, understood to mean rising up or climbing up.
Cooroy: from kurui, possum. Cooroibah: kurui-ba, place of possums.
Tewantin: usually traced to dauwadhan, often translated as dead trees or logs.
Koala: recorded as goala (F.J. Watson's 1944 vocabulary of the Kabi language).
Spellings vary because the languages were spoken, not written.

detail_blocks.text: More place names around our tours and rides:

items: Mt Cooran: from Guran, tall trees.
Mt Cooroora: a brush tail possum.
Lake Cootharaba: the place where wood for notched or studded clubs was found.
Doonan: thought to mean leaf of a tree.
Eumundi: after Ngumundi (or Huomundy), an Aboriginal leader said to have adopted the escaped convict Bracefield as his son in 1831.
Gympie: the Kabi Kabi name for a stinging tree that grew all around the Mary River.
Maroochydore: from Murukutchi-dha, place of the black swan.
Teewah: from Dauwah, dead wood or dry timber.
Tewantin: timber brought the first Europeans here, and felled logs were rafted to a sawmill on Lake Doonella in the 1860s, so a name meaning dead trees or logs fits.
Mt Tinbeerwah: place of grasstrees, or high hill climbing up.

sources: Sunshine Coast Council, Place Name Origins, https://heritage.sunshinecoast.qld.gov.au/Museums-and-Places/Place-Name-Origins ; Gubbi Gubbi Dyungungoo, https://gubbigubbidyungungoo.com/ ; F.J. Watson, Vocabularies of Four Representative Tribes of South Eastern Queensland (1944), Kabi entry "Goa'la or koa'la, or koa'dla, native bear".
